clue.text: Pitch for all the players

blocks.note: first meaning: to throw or fling
second meaning: every actor in a production

explanation.surface: A sports pitch shared by every member of the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' and 'players' suggest a sports field, but one is a verb for throwing and the other is the company of a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast is to throw, and the cast is the full list of performers in a play or film.

clue.text: There's much talk from me about mad character on TV

blocks.note: c. (circa) is Latin for about
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland
the box is slang for television

explanation.surface: A talkative presenter boasts about playing a crazy role on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is written in the answer's own voice: a person who says 'there's much talk from me' is describing themself.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterbox is a person who talks incessantly, which is what the speaker of the definition admits to.

clue.text: Volley in Oval's out of place?

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are not where they belong, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A cricket shot at the Oval goes astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, which makes 'Volley' look like a sporting stroke; here it is a burst of gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, the same as a volley of shots.

clue.text: Her husband's often away - word is, wag's worried

indicators.note: worried means troubled or shaken up, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Gossip says a footballer's partner frets because her husband is never home.
explanation.walkthrough: A WAG is a footballer's wife or girlfriend in British tabloid slang, which fits the scene of an absent husband.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass widow is a woman whose husband is frequently absent, for work or sport, leaving her alone.

clue.text: Disc on new label - sound familiar?

indicators.note: something new is made fresh, so these letters are formed into a different arrangement

blocks.note: a ring is a disc-shaped band
the letters of label rearranged

explanation.surface: A record released on a new label strikes a chord with listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' places the first piece above the second. 'Disc' and 'label' suggest records, but the disc is just a round shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring a bell is the idiom for seeming vaguely familiar, as a half-remembered name does.

clue.text: Small point, say

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a peak is a pointed summit

explanation.surface: A minor matter, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like the usual 'for example' signal, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something is to speak it, a direct synonym for uttering words.

clue.text: Sporting arena with the ultimate in football on display inside?

definitions.text: Sporting arena with the ultimate in football on display inside?

indicators.note: ultimate means final, so only the closing letter of the next word is taken
things set out on display are arranged anew for show, so these letters are laid out in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the final letter of football

explanation.surface: A stadium where the very best football is played.
explanation.walkthrough: WHITE HART LANE was the London ground of Tottenham Hotspur. The whole clue both defines the stadium and supplies the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: White Hart Lane was Tottenham Hotspur's football stadium, a sporting arena where top-flight matches were staged.

clue.text: Understands about Italian boxer and medicinal drug

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around what follows

blocks.note: to dig something is slang for understanding or liking it
IT is a standard abbreviation for Italian
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that an Italian fighter is taking medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian and the boxer join together, then sit inside the word for understands, which splits as DIG...S.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis, made from foxglove, is a medicine used to treat heart conditions.

clue.text: Possessing ingenuity, lead in Hamlet

indicators.note: the lead is the front runner, so only the first letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: wit is cleverness or ingenuity
the opening letter of Hamlet

explanation.surface: A clever actor taking the lead role in Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead in Hamlet' reads as the starring part, but it is just the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: With can mean having or possessing, as in 'a man with money'.

clue.text: Album by 1 Across - an announcement at 19, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: the 1995 debut record by the Liverpool band Cast
second meaning: what passengers hear when a train terminates at a station

explanation.surface: A band's album is broadcast as a railway announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 Across is CAST, a Britpop band; 19 is a London rail terminus, where everyone must leave the train at the end of the line.
explanation.definitionFit: All Change was Cast's first album, and it is the call telling passengers they must alight at the terminus.

clue.text: Listen to all the LP, as good judges do

blocks.note: first meaning: play both faces of a vinyl record
second meaning: consider each party's case fairly

explanation.surface: Fair judges play a long-playing record right through.
explanation.walkthrough: An LP is a vinyl record with two faces, so listening to all of it means playing both.
explanation.definitionFit: To give each party in a dispute a fair hearing is the idiom for impartiality, the mark of a good judge.

clue.text: Bar of gold I obtained around noon

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the preceding words wrap the next one

blocks.note: I + got, the past tense of obtain
N is an abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A prospector boasts of getting a gold bar at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, typically the bar shape in which gold is stored.

clue.text: Went to rear of orchestra pit and played second fiddle?

definitions.text: Went to rear of orchestra pit

blocks.clueFragment: Went to rear of orchestra pit
blocks.note: first meaning: literally sat in a seat at the back
second meaning: accepted a subordinate role

explanation.surface: A violinist moved to the back of the pit and took the lesser part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second fiddle' fits the orchestra picture, but here it is the idiom for being subordinate.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a back seat is to accept a less prominent role, just as playing second fiddle means being subordinate.

clue.text: Loner plays foolishly, in my opinion

indicators.note: acting foolishly means behaving without order, so these letters lose their sequence

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a solitary person is behaving foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Personally, used as a sentence adverb, introduces one's own view, the same as saying in my opinion.

clue.text: Iberis spread across lake? That's ludicrous

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so these letters are dispersed into a new order
spread across means stretched over something, so the reworked letters straddle the next piece

blocks.note: the letters of Iberis rearranged
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A garden flower growing all over a lake would be absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: Iberis, or candytuft, is a garden flowering plant; its letters are scrambled and then wrapped around the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Risible means laughable or absurd, so something risible is ludicrous.

clue.text: Drunken bum's greed overwhelmed

indicators.note: a drunken walk lurches all over the place, so these letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A drunk tramp's appetite got the better of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Submerged means flooded or covered by water, and so swamped or overwhelmed.

clue.text: A fool, cleaner to tell tales

blocks.note: a char, or charlady, is a British cleaning woman
telling tales can mean telling untruths

explanation.surface: A silly cleaning lady is a gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tell tales' suggests informing on someone, but here it means fibbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlie is British slang for a silly person, as in 'a right charlie'.

clue.text: Heavenly, Castile, rebuilt to enthral the Spanish

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again differently, so these letters are reassembled
to enthral is to hold captive, so the reworked letters hold the next piece within them

blocks.note: the letters of Castile rearranged
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A restored Spanish region charms its people divinely.
explanation.walkthrough: Castile is a historic kingdom of central Spain; the Spanish article sits after the first letter of the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial means of the sky or of heaven, so it is a synonym for heavenly.

clue.text: The M25, say - what's said about small section?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: oral means spoken
a bit is a small part

explanation.surface: Talk about a short stretch of London's motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M25 is the motorway that rings London; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital road circles a city, and the M25 is the classic British example encircling London.

clue.text: Water lilies - many round practice

indicators.note: round means encircling, so the first word wraps the second

blocks.note: lots means many
use means custom or practice

explanation.surface: Plenty of water lilies surround a training session.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water plant related to the water lily, and the name is applied to several such species.

clue.text: Awfully ostentatious name for a rail terminus

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are treated badly and end up in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A railway terminus has been given a terribly showy name.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston is a main London rail terminus serving the north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston Station is a London terminus, the end of the West Coast Main Line.

clue.text: With a spherical shape, bored out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A round object has been hollowed out by drilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bored out' reads as drilled hollow, but 'out' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbed is a poetic adjective meaning formed into an orb, a sphere.

clue.text: Perfect suggestion over learner driver

blocks.note: an idea is a suggestion or proposal
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: An excellent tip passed on to someone learning to drive.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the first piece above the second. L-plates mark a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, the best possible, the same as perfect.

clue.text: Girl is touring Rhode Island

indicators.note: touring means travelling around, so the first word goes around the next

blocks.note: taken as written
RI is the US postal code for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A young woman is travelling around a small American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a woman's first name, so it stands for a girl in crossword style.

clue.text: Soldier breaking free completely

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the first piece sits inside the next

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: A soldier makes a total escape from captivity.
explanation.walkthrough: Rigid as an adverb is informal: to be bored rigid or scared rigid means utterly so.
explanation.definitionFit: In idioms like 'scared rigid' the word works as an intensifier meaning utterly.

clue.text: Groom's partner, in good health in gaol

blocks.note: the bride marries the groom
well means healthy

explanation.surface: A newly married woman is fit and well despite being in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like part of 'in good health' and part of 'in gaol'; only one is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell was a London prison, and the name became a general word for a jail or house of correction.

clue.text: Teams go off demonstrating a way of riding

blocks.note: sides are teams in a match
eggs that addle go bad

explanation.surface: Teams leave the field to put on an equestrian display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' reads as departing, but it means turn rotten, as an egg does.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting side-saddle, with both legs on one side of the horse, is a traditional style of horseback riding.

clue.text: Drama in parking place

blocks.note: P is the road sign for parking
to lay is to put or place

explanation.surface: A dramatic scene unfolds in a car park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, but it only joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a dramatic work written for the stage.
